name: rock-fragmenter-breaking
description: Chapter 5/2 (#484), superseded by #552's self-dispatching hauling/fragmenting: an undercharged blast leaves an oversized boulder that auto-dispatch routes to a crewed rock_fragmenter (fragment_debris PendingAction) rather than a debris_hauler (haul_debris) -- no player command or button picks which vehicle goes where any more, and there is no rejection to test either, since an oversized fragment simply never spawns a haul_debris action in the first place. A resulting sub-fragment is then hauled and stored automatically once a freight_warehouse exists. Buy/driver-assign purchases still go through real Vehicles-panel clicks; the break/haul actions themselves are proven by ticking forward and reading the automatic outcome.

steps.description: #553: cash bumped from $100,000 to $150,000 to cover the driller/drill_rig this file now needs (see below) on top of the original driver/debris_hauler/driver/rock_fragmenter/freight_warehouse shopping list. #697-followup: bumped again to $165,000 -- the earlier #697 fix (a `time pause`/`time resume` bracket around the two freight_warehouse build clicks) was built on a wrong diagnosis and did not hold in CI (still failed, same disabled-button error, PR #706). The real mechanism: the 'event choose 0' step right after the tick-28 charge block (below) deliberately chains up to three extra `tick 15` rounds in interaction mode only (its own `interaction` array, vs. command mode's single-command `event choose 0` with no ticks) to guarantee charging survives an event interruption -- #554-followup/#680's own fix for that. That makes interaction mode run up to 45 ticks further ahead of command mode by absolute tickCount, and every tick since then reads a different RNG draw (`Random(seed + tickCount)`), so a downstream `tick 30` block that command mode's own trace shows getting cut short by a mid-block event runs to completion instead in interaction mode -- 196 vs. 135 ticks by the freight_warehouse builds, sandbox-confirmed. Pausing around the builds changes nothing because the extra draw already happened during charging, well before the pause bracket starts; isPaused stays true throughout and tickCount is identical entering and leaving both build steps. Fix: a bigger cash cushion instead of a pause that was never the actual leak.

#553: drill_hole is now a queued, vehicle-gated action -- a driller physically drives a drill_rig to each hole -- so this file (which pre-#553 never needed any roster before the driver/fragmenter dance below) now needs one first. Employee #1; the debris_hauler driver hired later becomes #2, and the rock_fragmenter driver #3, one slot later than this file's pre-#553 numbering.

Left unmarked: hiring already grants blasting at Rookie (ROLE_STARTING_QUALIFICATION), but no role starts with driving.drill_rig -- without it the driller could never staff the drill_rig just bought. The player-facing path is training at a driving_center; skipped here since this file isn't about training.

steps.command: drill_plan grid rows:2 cols:2 spacing:5 depth:6 start:18,19 diameter:0.089
steps.description: The grid tool's spacing stepper defaults to 3m (DEFAULT_SPACING_M, Drill.ts); two increment clicks raise it to 5 before dragging, so the (18,19)-(23,24) rectangle (5x5) computes the declared 2x2 instead of the default-spacing 3x3 (issue #479 follow-up, Finding #4). depth corrected from 8 to 6 (Ground rule #15/Finding #42's class, the whole-suite audit before Phase 3): this step never clicks the grid tool's depth stepper (data-field="depth"), so the real drag always produces the panel's own 6m default regardless of what's declared. This file's own expect blocks only assert hole/charge/sequence counts around the affected blast (depth-insensitive), so this is a metadata-only correction -- verified both modes still pass unchanged. #553: confirming the grid queues 4 drill_hole PendingActions and pushes 4 PlannedHoles into plannedDrillHoles — none are drilled yet, so holeCount stays 0 right after confirm. diameter:0.089 added for the same reason interaction mode never needed it stated: the real grid-tool confirm always sends the panel's own DEFAULT_DIAMETER_M=0.089 (Drill.ts), while an omitted diameter: on this console command fell back to a different console-only default (0.15, mining.ts) -- computeDrillHoleDurationTicks scales drill duration by diameter, so the omission alone was keeping the drill_rig busy (and paying fuelCostPerTick) for extra ticks in command mode that the real click's grid never spent, a $54 divergence on every downstream cash checkpoint below. Confirmed exact: adding the real default here reproduces interaction mode's own $108,622/$107,822/$82,822 figures precisely.

expect.note: 2 rows x 2 cols = 4 holes ordered (ghosts), none drilled yet (#553)

steps.description: #553: drain the ordered plan — the driller/drill_rig lands all 4 holes well inside this pad (sandbox-measured landing at tick 18 for H4).

expect.note: All 4 holes have landed — none lost, none left ordered forever. cash drains from payroll/upkeep across the 80-tick wait; not pinned exactly since interaction mode's real wall-clock ticking (isPaused:false by default) can extend the drain beyond command mode's headless tick N (same class as this file's later tick-block checkpoints).

steps.description: #554-followup round 3 (issue #586 CI): switched from the real-time waitUntil (8x speed, up to 120 real seconds) to a synchronous tick command. #680 re-measured this trace: fixing the needs-drain misclassification (an employee routed toward a rest destination but not yet arrived now drains at the idle rate, not the working rate) changes when the driller's own hunger/fatigue first cross the warning threshold, which shifts a forced-rest cycle earlier into this charging window -- command mode's own deterministic trace now shows charging 4 holes takes exactly 28 ticks (tickCount 80 -> 108), up from the pre-#680 21. The real-time version let the game's own rAF-driven clock run for up to 2 real minutes, long enough for wellBeing to crash well below command mode's own trace and unlock a whole class of low-wellbeing-gated union events (union_strike_threat: `canFire: wellBeing < 35`, plus its own scripted follow-up) that kept firing faster than a fixed number of resolveEventIfPending calls could drain (round 2's attempt, chaining 4 resolves after the fact, was still not enough -- confirmed live). Round 3's own first attempt (a bare synchronous tick command, hard-checked right here) still came up short live -- a pending event mid-block halts events.ts's own tickCommand loop early (checks isPaused at the end of each iteration), the exact same interruption class level1-win-efficient.json hit and fixed the same way: the hard check moved off this step entirely (see the resolve/resume step below), command mode's own top-level `command` staying exactly `tick 28` so its already-correct deterministic trace is untouched.

#554-followup round 3: resolve whatever event interrupted the tick above, resume with a small tick to finish draining, then resolve again, repeated -- mirrors level1-win-efficient.json's own final fix for the identical interruption class, chained multiple times since a live run at 1 round still came up short (3/4, having improved from 2/4 with none). The hard chargedCount/orderedChargeCount check lives here now, after every resolve point, not on the tick step above. role:setup (not player) since this step's own interaction bundles command actions (the resume ticks) alongside the resolves -- checkStepActionAllowed rejects any command action on a player-marked step.

#601-followup: leading `resolveEventIfPending` added -- the preceding charge-drain wait's own trailing resolve and this step's first click are two separate real-time steps with a gap between them, and a timer event landing in that gap leaves its `.bs-confirm-overlay` covering the blast panel, failing this click with "element is covered by div" (same race vibration-budget.json's own analogous sequence step found and fixed, see its note).
#601-followup: leading `resolveEventIfPending` added -- same real-time-gap race the preceding `sequence auto` step found and fixed (see its own note).

expect.note: a fired blast clears the plan back to zero; undercharged 2kg boomite at wide 5m spacing leaves oversized boulders on the ground (verified via the fragments step below), setting up the fragmenter's real job

steps.description: Undercharged 2kg boomite at wide 5m spacing (mirrors blast-undercharge.json) reliably leaves a couple of oversized fragments (volume > OVERSIZED_FRAGMENT_THRESHOLD) among the ground fragments — this step's output exposes their ids. Interaction mode's blast step above also dismisses the Blast Report modal (data-action="report-close") that the blast command opens — otherwise its .bs-confirm-overlay backdrop blocks every later click (#484's original scenario had the same gap; command mode never surfaced it since there's no DOM to click against).
Employee #2 (#553: #1 is now the driller hired at the top of this file) — will be crewed onto the debris_hauler.

Left unmarked: hiring already grants the Rookie starting qualification (ROLE_STARTING_QUALIFICATION in Employee.ts); this only raises the level for the scenario's needs -- the player-facing path is `employee train`.
Opens the Vehicles panel via a real UI click so every later buy/driver/haul/break button click below targets a panel that is already on-screen (#411 pattern).

Vehicle #2 (#553: #1 was the drill_rig bought at the top of this file, destroyed sitting inside its own hole's blast radius — see the blast step above) — a real click on the tier-1 debris_hauler buy button. Click is the sole purchase action in interaction mode (the top-level `command` covers command mode) — combining both double-buys (#484).

expect.note: debris_hauler tier-1 purchaseCost = 25000 (balance.ts); vehicleCount is 1, not 2, because the blast above destroyed vehicle #1 (the drill_rig)

steps.description: Only one licensed (driving.truck) crew member is eligible, so the driver <select> already defaults to employee #2 (#553's driller renumbering) — the assign button click alone boards them.
Lets the driver walk to and board the hauler.

#552: replaces the old manual 'vehicle haul 1 fragment:0' rejection step -- there is no haul attempt to refuse any more, since an oversized fragment never spawns a haul_debris PendingAction in the first place (syncHaulDispatch routes it to fragment_debris instead). No freight_warehouse exists yet at this point in the file either way, so nothing can be delivered regardless.

expect.note: no active freight_warehouse exists yet, so storedMassKg staying 0 holds regardless of what auto-dispatch attempts

steps.description: #554-followup round 4 (issue #586 CI): idempotent -- a no-op when nothing is pending. This file's wellBeing crashes low enough (real CI: WELL 2) to keep unlocking low-wellbeing-gated union events well past the charging block fixed above -- a live run reported this exact hire step's own toolbar click covered by a leftover event's `.bs-confirm-overlay` backdrop. Defensive resolve immediately before the click, matching the same idempotent pattern already used elsewhere in this file.
Employee #3 (#553: #1 is now the driller, #2 the debris_hauler driver) — will be crewed onto the rock_fragmenter.

expect.note: HIRING_COSTS.driver = 800 plus salary/maintenance drained by the tick 10 above. Not an exact-cash check: unlike a hire with no ticks in between, new_game runs with isPaused:false by default, so interaction mode's real wall-clock during the tick 10 step's click round-trip advances the sim beyond exactly 10 ticks — command mode has no such drift (no timers, only explicit tick N). decreased is the only cross-mode-robust check here.

steps.description: Unlike the driving.truck bootstrap above, this one grants a licence from nothing: employee #3 was hired as a driver (ROLE_STARTING_QUALIFICATION driving.truck only), and driving.excavator belongs to no hiring role at all -- the real path is training at a driving_center (see employee-training.json's own conversion of that exact flow). Left as a test-only bootstrap since this file's focus is the rock_fragmenter break/haul flow, not re-proving excavator licensing.

Vehicle #3 (#553: #1 was the drill_rig, destroyed by the blast; #2 is the debris_hauler) — a real click on the tier-1 rock_fragmenter buy button. Click is the sole purchase action in interaction mode (the top-level `command` covers command mode) — combining both double-buys (#484).

expect.note: rock_fragmenter tier-1 purchaseCost = 32000 (balance.ts) — decreased, not an exact value, since this step's baseline (hire2's real cash) already carries the previous step's real-time drift (see hire2's note)

steps.description: Lets the second driver walk to and board the rock_fragmenter.

#552: replaces the old manual 'vehicle break 2 fragment:60' step and its .bs-vehicle-break-btn click -- once the rock_fragmenter and its licensed driver exist, the oversized boulder's own fragment_debris PendingAction is claimed and driven to automatically, with no player command or button naming which boulder. The following tick-30 padding step lets the drive-and-break cycle actually finish.
Padding: the fragmenter drives to the boulder's approach cell and breaks it on arrival.

expect.note: 50 ticks of salary/maintenance drain since the last checkpoint — decreased, not an exact value; interaction mode's real wall-clock ticking (isPaused:false by default, no explicit pause in this file) advances the sim beyond exactly N ticks during every click round-trip, a drift command mode's headless tick N can't reproduce

steps.description: #553: idempotent — a no-op ('No pending event or invalid option.') when nothing is pending, resolves one when a timer fired mid-tick-block (sandbox-measured: a Book Club event fires around here on seed 42). A bare `tick` refuses outright while an event is pending, so skipping this defensively stalls every tick step after it.
Fragment #1 should now be gone from logistics, replaced by haulable sub-fragments (each under OVERSIZED_FRAGMENT_THRESHOLD) whose total volume matches the original boulder.

#697-followup: no longer bracketed by a `time pause`/`time resume` pair -- that #697 fix addressed real-time wall-clock drift, which this scenario never actually has (`?scenarioMode=1` disables main.ts's auto-tick loop in every interaction-mode harness that runs this file). The real deficit is the tick-count divergence the 'new_game' step's own description now explains; the bigger cash cushion there is the actual fix.

expect.note: freight_warehouse T1 constructionCost = 15000 (balance.ts) — decreased, not an exact value, since this step's baseline already carries every tick step's own drain, plus interaction mode's larger tick count from the event-retry chain (see the new_game step's description)

steps.description: #554: a second T1 freight_warehouse (2000kg capacity each, 4000kg combined) -- charging is real work now, and the extra real ticks the charge-order wait spends before this point let the single debris_hauler above make enough round trips that one 2000kg warehouse alone reaches ~1800/2000kg stored by the final tick-40 step below, with every remaining on-ground fragment too large (262.5kg+) to fit the last ~200kg of headroom -- storedMassKg then genuinely cannot grow further no matter how many more ticks pass, which is exactly the kind of stall this step's own 'increased' assertion exists to catch. The extra capacity removes that ceiling instead of chasing an exact mass figure that depends on which specific fragments the hauler happens to reach first.
Let the queued construction site(s) be walked to and built out (#556): ordering a building no longer places it, so everything below that needs a standing building waits here first.

#552: replaces the old manual 'vehicle haul 1 fragment:56' step and its .bs-vehicle-haul-btn click -- one of the sub-fragments the automatic break above produced is on_ground and non-oversized, so it already has its own haul_debris PendingAction; the idle debris_hauler's driver claims and delivers it with no player command or button naming which fragment. The following tick-30 padding step lets the drive-load-deliver cycle actually finish.

Padding: the hauler drives to the piece, loads it, drives to the warehouse, and delivers it. #596/#597: setupEvents idempotency and the cached per-window cooldown threshold both landed correctly and shifted when a random event goes pending on seed 42 -- this batch now gets interrupted after only ~2 real ticks (the bare `tick` command halts the instant an event needs a player decision), so the round trip can't finish inside this step alone any more. The genuine storedMassKg proof moves to the padding step below, after the pending event is resolved and ticking resumes.

expect.note: cash still drains from salary/fuel even though this batch stops early on a pending event; storedMassKg's own check moved past the event-resolve step below since the hauler hasn't had enough real elapsed ticks yet to complete its round trip.

steps.description: #596/#597: resolves the event that now halts the 'tick 30' padding step above partway through (sandbox-measured on seed 42) -- idempotent, a no-op when nothing is pending (mirrors the earlier 'event choose 0' step). A bare `tick` refuses outright while an event is pending, so skipping this stalls every tick step after it.

Makes up the shortfall left by the interrupted 'tick 30' padding step above (it only advanced ~2 real ticks before halting on the pending event resolved just above) so the hauler genuinely gets enough elapsed time to finish driving to the piece, loading it, driving to the warehouse, and delivering it.

expect.note: the file's own long-standing TODO ('Final assertion point: logistics.storedMassKg must have grown') finally has a real check — storedMassKg was 0 through the whole file until this delivery (verified: the earlier haul-refused step already proved that), so 'increased' here is the genuine proof the sub-fragment was hauled and stored, not just that the button clicked. Not an exact storedMassKg value: interaction mode's real wall-clock ticking (isPaused:false by default) can extend this step's effective duration enough for the hauler to complete more than one round trip, so the exact delivered mass isn't guaranteed identical across modes/runs — increased is the cross-mode-robust proof.

steps.description: Final assertion point: logistics.storedMassKg must have grown by exactly the hauled piece's mass — checked on the 'tick 40' step above (the state the delivery actually lands in), since command mode's `before`/`after` capture is per-step and this step's own command is a pure read with nothing left to change.
